transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. For a Bosch condenser dryer like yours, damp clothes after two hours is most often caused by restricted airflow rather than a broken part. A clogged lint filter or dirty condenser stops the hot air from circulating, which prevents drying and can trip safety cut-outs. 1. Clean the main lint filter in the door frame.
2. Open the flap at the bottom front, remove the condenser unit, rinse it under a tap until clean, let it drip dry, and put it back.
3. Run a normal cotton programme for 10 minutes and check if the drum gets warm. Let me know if they were dirty/clean and whether you felt heat.
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check" — If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]

ok, filter in the door had fluff and a waxy film, rinsed it and water barely passes through until I scrubbed it. never cleaned the condenser before, front of it was matted with lint but it came clean with the shower head. it's hot inside the drum after 20 min. should I run a test cycle now?

[Heading: Airflow restriction (cleaned)]
That explains the poor drying: the waxy film and fluff were blocking airflow, which stops heat from circulating effectively. Please run a test cycle now using a medium load on a standard cotton programme. If the clothes come out damp again, wipe the two metal strips inside the door frame (near where the filter was) with a little vinegar or rubbing alcohol to remove any remaining coating.
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer not drying properly — what to check" — Poor drying is most often caused by restricted airflow. Clean the fluff filter every cycle, clean the condenser regularly and avoid overloading the drum — these are safe checks you can do yourself. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]
ok, running a test cycle now with a normal load. will report back

That sounds like a solid start. The waxy film and fluff were definitely choking the airflow, so cleaning them should have restored the drying performance. Please let me know how the test cycle went—did the clothes come out dry, or are they still damp?
test cycle done. clothes came out dry in about 100 minutes and the water container is nearly full now.

[Heading: Restricted airflow due to dirty lint filter and condenser]
That is excellent news. The damp clothes were caused by the blocked lint filter and condenser restricting airflow, which prevented the dryer from circulating hot air effectively. To keep it running well, try to clean the lint filter after every cycle and rinse the condenser unit out every few months or whenever you notice the drying time increasing again.
